sections.text: About Millionaire for Life™
Millionaire for Life™ is a multi-state daily draw game. Play for your chance to win $1,000,000 a year for LIFE!
How To Play

Millionaire for Life costs $5 per play and has the HIGHEST daily jackpot in lottery history. Choose 5 out of 58 numbers for the white balls, then pick your Millionaire Ball™ number from 1 to 5. You can choose your own numbers or ask for an Easy Pick to have the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to select the numbers on your ticket. Check the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 10 consecutive drawings at a time. Millionaire for Life drawings are held daily at approximately 10:15 p.m. Here in Iowa, tickets may be purchased until 8:59 p.m. each day.
Prizes & Odds

The set prize amounts for the top prize and tier 2 prize published here are based on the expected number of winners sharing in the prize pool. In some cases, these prizes may be paid on a pari-mutuel basis and will be lower than these prize levels.
There are nine prize levels in the game. Millionaire for Life prizes won in Iowa must be claimed within 180 days of the drawing in which they were won.
Millionaire for Life Top and Tier 2 Prize Options

Millionaire for Life’s top two prize levels are described as “lasting as long as you do,” meaning that they are truly for life. The minimum guaranteed payout for those two prize levels is 20 years, and there is a lump-sum option for players who prefer that rather than lifetime annuity payments
Top Prize

rows: $1 Million a year for life divided*

sections.text: Tier 2 Prize
*A minimum annuitized prize value is $50,000 per year for life. **See game rules Section 6.C. Prize Liability Limitation.

Players have 60 days from the date they claim their prize to choose the cash or annuity payment option. Prizes that are governed by "split-prize" liability are divided equally among the winning tickets and may be less than shown.
For further details, see the official Game Rules .
History

Millionaire for Life launched Feb. 22, 2026, in Iowa and 30 other jurisdictions. The game joined the Multi-State Lottery Association (MUSL) lineup, which also includes Powerball and Lotto America in Iowa.
Examples of Winning Combinations

rows: Select three numbers (unique or not) to match the winning numbers in the order that they were picked. Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3, only exact order plays of 1-2-3 are winners.

Pick three unique numbers to match the winning numbers in any order. There are six ways to win (six possible combinations). Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3, any plays with those numbers (such as 3-2-1) are winners.

Pick three numbers -- two of which are identical -- to match the winning numbers in any order. There are three ways to win (three possible combinations). Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-1-2, any plays with those numbers (such as 1-2-1) are winners.

Pick two numbers to match the first two winning numbers in the order that they were picked. Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3, only exact order plays of those first two numbers (1-2-x) are winners.

Pick two numbers to match the last two winning numbers in the order that they were picked. Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3, only exact order plays of those last two numbers (x-2-3) are winners.

sections.text: Examples of Winning Combinations

rows: Pick any four numbers (unique or not) to match the winning numbers in the order that they were picked. Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3-4, only exact order plays of 1-2-3-4 are winners.

Pick four unique numbers to match the winning numbers in any order. There are 24 ways to win (24 possible combinations). Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3-4, any plays with those numbers (such as 3-2-4-1) are winners.

Pick four numbers -- two of which are identical -- to match the winning numbers in any order. There are 12 ways to win (12 possible combinations). Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-1-3, any plays with those numbers (such as 3-1-1-2) are winners.

Pick four numbers -- two pairs of identical numbers -- to match the winning numbers in any order. There are six ways to win (six possible combinations). Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-1-2, any plays with those numbers (such as 2-1-1-2) are winners.

Pick four numbers -- three of which are identical -- to match the winning numbers in any order. There are four ways to win (four possible combinations). Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-1-1-2, any plays with those numbers (such as 1-2-1-1) are winners.

Pick two numbers to match the first two winning numbers in the order that they were picked. Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3-4, only exact order plays of those first two numbers (1-2-x-x) are winners.

Pick two numbers to match the last two winning numbers in the order that they were picked. Example: If the winning numbers were picked 1-2-3-4, only exact order plays of those last two numbers (x-x-3-4) are winners.

sections.text: About Powerball
Powerball® is a multi-state game known for giant jackpots. You could win millions or even billions when you play!
How To Play

It's easy. Pick five numbers from 1 to 69. Pick a separate Powerball number from 1 to 26. The more numbers you match in a drawing, the more you win. If you match all six winning numbers, you win the jackpot!

Choose your own numbers or request an easy pick for the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to pick the numbers for you. Select the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 10 consecutive drawings at a time.
Powerball drawings are held Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays at 9:59 p.m. Tickets can be purchased until 8:59 p.m. on the evening of the drawing.
Powerball prizes won in Iowa must be claimed within 180 days of the drawing in which they were won.
Power Play Option
You can add the Power Play option to your Powerball ticket for the chance to multiply most prizes by up to 10 times.

For an extra $1 for the Power Play, you could increase your prize amount (except the jackpot and Match 5 prize) by 2, 3, 4, 5 or 10 times (10X multiplier is used only when the jackpot is $150 million or less).
Prize Payouts & Odds including Power Play (PP) Option**
Prize Payouts & Odds for Powerball Double Play

The Double Play feature gives you the chance to play – and win – with the same set of numbers in two drawings rather than just one. For an extra $1 per play, the numbers on your ticket are eligible to win in the regular Powerball drawing and a separate Double Play drawing with a top cash prize of $10 million.
You could win a prize in both drawings on the same night.
The Double Play drawing is held after every Powerball drawing on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays.

Players can add both the Power Play and Double Play options to their tickets, in which case, a Powerball play would cost $4. While Power Play multiplies Powerball winnings at all prize levels except the jackpot, it does not apply to Double Play winnings.
Cash Option vs. Annuity Option

When a player wins the Powerball jackpot, they can choose to receive the prize in annuity payments over time or take a lump-sum payment. A player has 60 days from the date they claim their prize in Iowa to choose the cash or annuity option.

If the player selects the cash option, they will receive a single payment equal to the amount available in the jackpot prize pool from the sale of tickets in the game. If the player chooses the annuity option, the prize will be paid in 30 payments over 29 years. The annual payment will increase by 5 percent to accommodate for factors such as inflation. If the cost to purchase the annuity is less than $250,000, the lottery may elect to pay the prize as "cash."
History
Powerball began in April 1992 and has grown into one of the world's largest and best-known lotto games. It offers big jackpots and the chance to win lots of other prizes, too.

The largest jackpot won in the game to date was a world-record prize of $2.04 billion in November 2022. The largest Powerball jackpot in Iowa was won in October 2018. Lerynne West of Redfield claimed that $343.9 million Powerball prize. West's ticket split the $687.8 million Powerball jackpot with a ticket in New York in the drawing on Oct. 27, 2018.

*The advertised jackpot is based on prize payment as an annuity. The jackpot prize will be divided equally among multiple winners based on the amount available to the lottery for the jackpot prize pool.

**The set prize amounts published here are based on the expected number of winners sharing in the prize pool. In some cases, these prizes may be paid on a pari-mutuel basis and will be lower than these prizes levels.
***The 10X multiplier is only used when the jackpot is $150 million or less.
About Mega Millions
Mega Millions is a multi-state lottery game with MEGA jackpots and MEGA fun.
How To Play

Choose five numbers from 1 to 70 for the white balls, then pick the yellow Mega Ball from a separate pool of 1 to 24. The more numbers you match in a drawing, the more you win. If you match all six numbers, you win the jackpot!

You can choose your own numbers or ask for an easy pick to have the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to select the numbers on your ticket. Check the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 10 consecutive drawings at a time.
There are nine prize levels in the game, so even if you don't win the jackpot, be sure to check your ticket after each drawing.

A multiplier is built into each play in the game, so any prize you win except the jackpot will be multiplied by 2X, 3X, 4X, 5X or even 10X. That means there are no break-even prizes. The smallest prize you can win in the game is $10 – twice the purchase price.
Prizes & Odds of Winning
The multiplier for each play is randomly assigned and automatically included. For tickets containing multiple plays, the multipliers on the ticket can repeat, be different, or all be the same.
The Mega Millions jackpot starts at $50 million and grows until someone wins it. Then it resets to the starting amount and begins to grow again.
Mega Millions drawings are held at 10 p.m. on Tuesdays and Fridays. Tickets can be purchased until 8:59 p.m. on the evening of the drawing.
Mega Millions prizes won in Iowa must be claimed within 180 days of the drawing in which they were won.
Cash vs. Annuity Option

A Mega Millions jackpot winner can choose to receive the prize in annuity payments over time or as a one-time, lump-sum payment. A player has 60 days from the date they claim their prize in Iowa to choose the cash or annuity option.
If the player selects the cash option, they will receive a single payment equal to the amount available in the jackpot prize pool from the sale of tickets in the game.

If the player chooses the annuity option, their prize will be paid in 30 payments over 29 years. The annual payment will increase by 5 percent to accommodate for factors like inflation. If the cost to purchase the annuity is less than $250,000, the lottery may elect to pay the prize as cash.
History

Mega Millions began on August 31, 1996, as the Big Game. In May 2002, the multi-state game was redesigned and given the new name of Mega Millions. Then in January 2010, 23 more state lotteries, including the Iowa Lottery, began selling Mega Millions.
The largest Mega Millions jackpot to date was a prize of more than $1.6 billion won in Florida in August 2023.

*The jackpot prize will be divided equally among multiple winners based on the amount available in the game’s jackpot prize pool. The game’s total prize pool is estimated to be 55 percent of Mega Millions sales, but may be higher or lower based upon the number of winners at each guaranteed prize level, as well as the funding required to meet the official advertised jackpot. The official Mega Millions grand prize annuity amount is subject to change based on sales forecasts and/or actual sales. Reminder: The multiplier does not apply to the jackpot.

**The set prize amounts published here are based on the expected number of winners sharing in the prize pool. For any drawing, if prize liability exceeds the percentage of the prize pool allocated to the set prize levels, then all prizes except the jackpot prize may become pari-mutuel and would be lower than these prize levels.
About Lotto America
Lotto America ® is today's version of the original lottery game from the 1980s that paved the way for big jackpots.
How To Play

Choose 5 out of 52 numbers for the white balls, then pick your Star Ball® number from 1 to 10. The more numbers you match in a drawing, the more you win. If you match all six numbers, you win the jackpot!

Choose your own numbers or request an easy pick for the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to select the numbers on your ticket. Check the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 10 consecutive drawings at a time.
All Star Bonus Option
You also have the option of adding the All Star Bonus to your Lotto America purchase! For an extra $1 for the All Star Bonus, you could multiply your prize (except the jackpot) by 2, 3, 4 or 5 times.
There are nine prize levels in the game, so be sure to check your ticket for any prize you may have won.
Prizes & Odds including the All Star Bonus Option**
Lotto America drawings are held at about 9:15 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays. Tickets can be purchased until 8:59 p.m. on the evening of the drawing.
Lotto America prizes won in Iowa must be claimed within 180 days of the drawing in which they were won.
Cash vs. Annuity Option

When a player wins the Lotto America jackpot, the winner can choose to receive the prize in annuity payments or elect to take a lump-sum payment. A player has 60 days from the date they claim their prize in Iowa to choose the cash or annuity option.

If the player selects the cash option, they will receive a single payment equal to the amount available in the jackpot prize pool from the sale of tickets in the game. If the player chooses the annuity option, the prize will be paid in 30 payments over 29 years. The annual payment will increase by 5 percent to accommodate for factors like inflation. If the cost to purchase the annuity is less than $250,000, the lottery may elect to pay the prize as cash.
For further details, click the Game Rules link at the top of this page.
History

Today's Lotto America is a throwback version of the first multi-state lotto game that became known for big jackpots in the United States. Iowa was a founding member of that original version of Lotto America, which began in 1988 and made headlines around the world at the time for its jackpots. That game ultimately was replaced by Powerball in 1992.

*The advertised jackpot is based on prize payment as an annuity. The jackpot prize will be divided equally among multiple winners based on the amount available to the lottery for the jackpot prize pool. The set prize amounts published here are based on the expected number of winners sharing in the prize pool. In some cases, these prizes may be paid on a pari-mutuel basis and will be lower than these prize levels.

**If the All Star Bonus option is purchased, prize(s) won increase 2, 3, 4 or 5 times depending on the multiplier number for that drawing. Jackpot prizes are not eligible for the All Star Bonus option.
About Powerball Xs & Os™
Powerball Xs & Os™ is a multi-state weekly draw game. Play for your chance to win cash prizes, football experiences in the second chance drawings and more!
How To Play*

Powerball Xs & Os™ is a draw-based game similar to other lotto games like Powerball and Millionaire for Life. It costs $5 per play and has the BEST ODDS of all the national draw games! The ticket prints straight from the terminal.

You can choose your own NFL team logos, 8 out of 32, or ask for an Easy Pick to have the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to select the teams on your ticket. Check the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 10 consecutive drawings at a time.
Powerball Xs & Os drawings are held weekly on Sundays at approximately 9:00 p.m. Here in Iowa, tickets may be purchased until 7:59 p.m. each day.
Powerball prizes won in Iowa must be claimed within 180 days of the drawing in which they were won.

The set prize amounts published herein are based upon the expected number of winners sharing the prize pool. In some cases, these prizes may be paid on a pari-mutuel basis and will be lower than the prize levels.
Prizes & Odds**
Cash Option vs. Annuity Option

Unlike Powerball, prizes, including the Jackpot Prize award, are cash only. There is no annuity option. The player will receive a single payment equal to the amount available in the jackpot prize pool from the sale of tickets in the game.
Points for Prizes at PowerballOfficial.com

Fans can enter both winning and nonwinning eligible tickets into the new national Powerball promotional prize program, featuring exclusive prize drawings. You can enter them as soon as you purchase them – there's no need to wait for the drawing!

Every ticket entered earns you points that you can enter for a chance to win the prizes you want most. Best of all, there is no additional cost to participate beyond the purchase of an eligible Powerball Xs & Os ticket.

Available prizes include a trip to Super Bowl LXI, NFL Shop gift cards to purchase their favorite NFL officially licensed products, and unique NFL experiences. Prize availability, details, and fulfillment are subject to the official rules.
For further details, see the official Powerball Xs & Os website. Powerball Xs & Os website
History

Powerball Xs & Os™ launched Sep. 8 2026, in Iowa and 23 other jurisdictions. The game joined the Multi-State Lottery Association (MUSL) lineup, which also includes Powerball, Millionaire for Life and Lotto America in Iowa.
*Powerball Xs & Os results are randomly drawn and not based on, determined by, or dependent on the outcome of NFL games.
****Jackpot and lower-tier prizes may become pari-mutuel in some circumstances.

Disclaimer: the Powerball Xs & Os game is operated by the lotteries that sell the game. The NFL, the NFL Properties LLC, and the NFL Members Clubs that comprise the National Football League are not sponsors of, or affiliated with the Powerball Xs & Os lottery game. NFL Team logos are licensed for use to the Multi-State Lottery Association, and any reproduction is strictly prohibited. By purchasing a Play/ticket for the Powerball Xs & Os Game, players are NOT playing the Powerball Game and are NOT placing bets on the outcome of any NFL game.
About Pick 3
Pick 3 is a daily game that leaves nearly all of the choices up to the player. With drawings twice a day, the prize you can win depends on the type of play you make.
How To Play
Pick 3 plays range in price from 50 cents up to $5. Choose three numbers, each from 0 through 9.

You can choose your own numbers or ask for an easy pick to have the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to select the numbers on your ticket. Check the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 16 consecutive drawings at a time.
You'll also select the type of play you want to make:

items: Straight - match all three numbers in the EXACT ORDER as drawn.
Box - match all numbers IN ANY ORDER.
Straight/Box - match all numbers in the EXACT and/or ANY ORDER.
Front Pair - match the first two numbers in the EXACT ORDER.
Back Pair - match the last two numbers in the EXACT ORDER.

sections.text: Prizes & Odds

Midday Pick 3 drawings are held at about 12:20 p.m. each day. Evening drawings are held daily at about 10 p.m. Tickets can be purchased until noon on the day of the drawing for midday drawings and until 9:40 p.m. on the day of the drawing for evening drawings.
Pick 3 prizes must be claimed within 90 days of the drawing in which they were won.
For further details, click the Game Rules link at the top of this page.
History
Pick 3 debuted in July 1998 in Iowa with evening drawings held Monday through Saturday. Midday drawings in the game were added in September 2003. Sunday drawings began in July 2010.
About Pick 4
Pick 4 is a daily game that leaves nearly all of the choices up to the player. With drawings twice a day, the prize you can win depends on the type of play you make.
How To Play
Pick 4 plays range in price from 50 cents up to $5. Choose four numbers, each from 0 through 9.

You can choose your own numbers or ask for an easy pick to have the lottery terminal or self-service kiosk to select the numbers on your ticket. Check the multi-draw box to buy tickets for up to 16 consecutive drawings at a time.
You'll also select the type of play you want to make:

items: Straight - match all numbers in the EXACT ORDER as drawn.
Box - match all four numbers IN ANY ORDER.
Straight/Box - match either EXACT and/or ANY ORDER.
Front Pair - match the first two numbers in the EXACT ORDER as drawn.
Back Pair - match the last two numbers in the EXACT ORDER as drawn.

sections.text: Prizes & Odds

Midday Pick 4 drawings are held at about 12:20 p.m. each day. Evening drawings are held at about 10 p.m. daily. Tickets can be purchased until noon on the day of the drawing for midday drawings and until 9:40 p.m. on the day of the drawing for evening drawings.
Pick 4 prizes must be claimed within 90 days of the drawing in which they were won.
For further details, click the Game Rules link at the top of this page.
History
Pick 4 debuted in September 2003 in Iowa with midday and evening drawings held Monday through Saturday. Sunday drawings in the game began in July 2010.
